## Introduction

Before the DataLab tasks, you completed a brief survey about:

- **Demographics**: Age, gender, handedness
- **Lifestyle**: Sleep, caffeine, exercise, screen time
- **Pre-task state**: Mood, energy, stress levels
- **Personality**: The Ten-Item Personality Inventory (TIPI)

::: {.key-finding}
#### Key Finding
Participants showed typical variation in Big Five personality traits, with **Agreeableness** and **Conscientiousness** scoring highest on average. Sleep quality was positively correlated with pre-task mood.
:::

## Demographics Overview

```{webr-r}
# Age distribution
ggplot(demog, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#3498db", color = "white") +
  labs(
    x = "Age",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Age Distribution",
    subtitle = paste("Mean age:", round(mean(demog$age), 1), "years")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

```{webr-r}
# Gender and handedness
demog |>
  count(gender) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = gender, y = n, fill = gender)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Male" = "#3498db", "Female" = "#e74c3c", "Other" = "#9b59b6")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Count", title = "Gender Distribution") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"))
```

## Sleep Patterns

```{webr-r}
ggplot(demog, aes(x = sleep_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = "#9b59b6", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 8, linetype = "dashed", color = "#e74c3c", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 8.2, y = 5, label = "Recommended\n(8 hours)",
           hjust = 0, color = "#e74c3c", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Hours of Sleep (Previous Night)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Sleep Duration",
    subtitle = paste("Mean:", round(mean(demog$sleep_hours), 1), "hours")
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"))
```

```{webr-r}
# Sleep quality vs mood
ggplot(demog, aes(x = sleep_quality, y = mood_pre)) +
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = 0.7, color = "#9b59b6", width = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#275882") +
  labs(
    x = "Sleep Quality (1-5)",
    y = "Pre-Task Mood (1-10)",
    title = "Does Sleep Quality Affect Mood?",
    subtitle = "Better sleep = better mood?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"))
```

```{webr-r}
# Correlation test
cor.test(demog$sleep_quality, demog$mood_pre)
```

## The Big Five Personality Traits

The **TIPI (Ten-Item Personality Inventory)** measures five personality dimensions:

| Trait | Items | Description |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| **Extraversion** | 1, 6R | Outgoing vs reserved |
| **Agreeableness** | 2R, 7 | Friendly vs critical |
| **Conscientiousness** | 3, 8R | Organised vs careless |
| **Emotional Stability** | 4R, 9 | Calm vs anxious |
| **Openness** | 5, 10R | Creative vs conventional |

*R = reverse scored (8 - score)*

```{webr-r}
# Calculate Big Five scores
demog <- demog |>
  mutate(
    extraversion = (tipi_1 + (8 - tipi_6)) / 2,
    agreeableness = ((8 - tipi_2) + tipi_7) / 2,
    conscientiousness = (tipi_3 + (8 - tipi_8)) / 2,
    emotional_stability = ((8 - tipi_4) + tipi_9) / 2,
    openness = (tipi_5 + (8 - tipi_10)) / 2
  )

# Summary
demog |>
  summarise(
    Extraversion = mean(extraversion),
    Agreeableness = mean(agreeableness),
    Conscientiousness = mean(conscientiousness),
    `Emotional Stability` = mean(emotional_stability),
    Openness = mean(openness)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Trait", values_to = "Mean") |>
  arrange(desc(Mean))
```

## Visualise Personality Profile

```{webr-r}
# Reshape for plotting
big5_long <- demog |>
  select(id, extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness,
         emotional_stability, openness) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = "trait",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  mutate(trait = factor(trait,
    levels = c("extraversion", "agreeableness", "conscientiousness",
               "emotional_stability", "openness"),
    labels = c("Extraversion", "Agreeableness", "Conscientiousness",
               "Emotional\nStability", "Openness")))

ggplot(big5_long, aes(x = trait, y = score, fill = trait)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 2, color = "#275882") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e74c3c", "#27ae60", "#3498db", "#f39c12", "#9b59b6")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 4, linetype = "dashed", color = "#275882") +
  annotate("text", x = 5.3, y = 4.2, label = "Midpoint", color = "#275882", size = 3) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Score (1-7)",
    title = "Big Five Personality Profile",
    subtitle = "Higher scores = more of that trait"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

## Pre-Task State

How were participants feeling before the lab?

```{webr-r}
# Pre-task mood, energy, stress
state_data <- demog |>
  select(id, mood_pre, energy_pre, stress_pre) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -id,
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "rating"
  ) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure,
    levels = c("mood_pre", "energy_pre", "stress_pre"),
    labels = c("Mood", "Energy", "Stress")))

ggplot(state_data, aes(x = measure, y = rating, fill = measure)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#27ae60", "#f39c12", "#e74c3c")) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Rating (1-10)",
    title = "Pre-Task Psychological State",
    subtitle = "How were you feeling before the lab?"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#275882", face = "bold")
  )
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The TIPI in Research

The **Ten-Item Personality Inventory** (Gosling et al., 2003) is a brief measure of the Big Five personality traits. While not as reliable as longer measures (like the 44-item BFI), it's useful for:

- **Time-limited studies** where personality is not the main focus
- **Large-scale surveys** where brevity is essential
- **Screening purposes** before more detailed assessment

Typical internal reliability (Cronbach's α) is lower than full inventories, but test-retest reliability is adequate for research purposes.
:::

---

::: {.key-finding}
#### Summary

The sample showed typical variation in Big Five personality traits. Sleep quality was positively associated with pre-task mood, highlighting the importance of rest for psychological well-being. The data provides a foundation for exploring how individual differences might relate to task performance.
:::
